items.title: Novartis pauses midstage Fabhalta trial in lupus nephritis—but efficacy, safety not at play
items.summary: Amid a steady advance of kidney-focused label expansions, Novartis’ Fabhalta is slowing its roll in a key potential autoimmune niche.

items.title: The Next Chapter for AI in Clinical Trials
items.summary: As agentic AI enters clinical development, governance and human judgment will determine its value.

items.title: Eli Lilly's Omvoh takes phase 3 win in pediatric UC, fueling expansion ambitions
items.summary: A new positive phase 3 readout in kids with ulcerative colitis could help Lilly's Omvoh gain a competitive edge against its IL-23 rivals.

items.title: Closing the gap between approval and treatment
items.summary: Lauren Boyer, CEO of Underscore, on why patient finding is a marketing job, and how to reach the people traditional data can't see.

items.title: Why Are 53% of Phase 2 and 3 Trials Delayed? A Redesign Is Overdue
items.summary: A different model can improve quality, speed, and cost at once.

items.title: GSK taps actress Viola Davis for shingles-focused campaign
items.summary: The "How to Get Away With Murder" star is the face of GSK's "Shingles, actually" campaign, which positions an increased shingles risk as an untold reality of aging.

items.title: Trump's pharma holdings surged as drugmakers benefited from Medicare price negotiation carveouts, Democrats allege
items.summary: As midterms loom, Democrats on Congress’ Joint Economic Committee (JEC) are reviving concerns about the orphan drug carveout tucked into Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, alleging that President Donald Trump accumulated millions of dollars in pharma stocks before and after the enactment of policies benefiting some of those same companies.

items.title: The Oral GLP-1 Tracker: Foundayo, Wegovy pill undergo minor fluctuations
items.summary: Fierce Pharma is launching the weekly Oral GLP-1 Tracker, leveraging analysts’ notes and IQVIA data to monitor prescription trends and shifting market shares as Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill and Eli Lilly's Foundayo vie to become the go-to oral weight-loss solution for millions.

items.title: Lilly's obesity pill, RevMed's pancreatic cancer breakthrough among slew of CHMP endorsements in Europe
items.summary: Across the pond, European regulators handed down a pair of pivotal approval recommendations this week, making way for a new front in Novo and Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 showdown and endorsing Revolution Medicines’ potential pancreatic cancer game changer.

items.title: Sanofi cycles deeper into sports marketing niche as Tour de France partner
items.summary: The French pharma will sponsor the prestigious white jersey, awarded to the best rider under 25, at both the Tour de France and the Tour de France Femmes in 2027.

items.title: Inside Teva's Weltruza launch and Novo's GLP-1 strategy
items.summary: This week on "The Top Line," we catch up with leaders from Teva and Novo to discuss new drug launches, growth opportunities and what's ahead for both companies.

items.title: Roche makes class-first push into thyroid eye disease with new FDA nod for Enspryng
items.summary: Some six years after scoring an initial FDA nod, Roche’s IL-6 receptor inhibitor Enspryng is muscling up to Amgen's Tepezza in a key eye disease arena.

items.title: Fierce Pharma Asia—Roche’s $1.2B obesity deal; Asahi Kasei’s FDA nod; Verastem’s KRAS boon
items.summary: Roche extended its China shopping spree with a $1 billion-plus obesity deal. Asahi Kasei's Hovilpri became the first HSV drug with a novel mechanism approved in nearly 30 years. Verastem's China-licensed KRAS G12D inhibitor showed strong early data in pancreatic cancer. And more.

items.title: Drugmakers, PhRMA seek to intervene in hospitals' 340B rebate challenge
items.summary: The American Hospital Association and others have launched a legal rematch with the federal government over the second iteration of a pilot program swapping out safety-net hospitals’ upfront drug discounts for after-the-fact rebates.

items.title: Kindeva lands $226M defense contract to supply nerve agent antidote in US
items.summary: Kindeva's Meridian was awarded a $226 million defense contract to supply the U.S. military with its self-injected nerve agent antidote and bolster national defense against chemical threats.

items.title: Par Health recalls 22 lots of IV blood thinner, its 3rd US product pull in a month
items.summary: Par Health issued a recall of 22 lots of the intravenous anticoagulant argatroban, the latest in a string of recent recalls related to IV-bag contamination risk.

items.title: With new Omvoh analyses, Lilly argues 'higher bar' for IBD treatment is within reach
items.summary: In the fiercely competitive inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) market, Eli Lilly is making the case for its antibody Omvoh as a holistic solution for patients living with ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease—and one that could offer relief after other biologic drugs have failed, too.

items.title: Gilead puts a timely spotlight on HIV prevention in Latino communities with 'Ahorita Mismo' campaign
items.summary: Gilead's “Ahorita Mismo (Right Now!)” stars two popular Latino creators in a call-in podcast-themed spot looking to spark conversations around HIV prevention.

items.title: Isotope supplier NorthStar continues rise with partnership to tee up China radiopharmaceutical filings
items.summary: As the momentum continues to pick up at NorthStar Medical Technologies, the radioisotope producer is strengthening ties in China, in a move that helps put its actinium-225 supplies on the map for local radiopharmaceutical filings.

items.title: Compass puts treatment-resistant depression on the map with first awareness day
items.summary: Compass Pathways has partnered with mental health organizations on the first-ever awareness day for treatment-resistant depression.

items.title: FDA clears ImmunityBio’s Anktiva expansion in bladder cancer after regulatory whiplash
items.summary: To expand Anktiva’s label, the FDA adopted a new approach to how it evaluates treatments for BCG-unresponsive NMIBC. The new regulatory path essentially allowed ImmunityBio to bypass an expensive randomized phase 3 trial that competitor Johnson & Johnson is currently forced to grind through.
